newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon Byblos bank results said "very good".
newsitem.headline: Lebanon Byblos bank results said "very good".

text.p: Beirut brokers said a 41.2 percent rise in mid-year profits to 23.015 billion Lebanese pounds ($14.9 million) reported by Byblos Bank was "very good" and met expectations.
However, they did not expect the results to have much impact on the bank's shares.
"It is much in line with expectations of $30 million net profits for the year," a broker who asked not to be identified told Reuters.
"The results are very good," another broker said.
A third broker said: "Since the results are not more than expected but rather as expected, I don't think they will have much impact on the price of the share."
"However, a good rating by Moody's might bring the prices up," he added.

Byblos said on Tuesday it had concluded a deal with Moody's Investors Service and would be rated by the end of July. It said it would also meet with the European credit rating agency IBCA to otain a rating.
The results compared with net profits of 16.293 billion pounds for the first half of 1996 and 8.5 billion pounds for the same period a year earlier.
"Byblos performance was maintained at relatively good levels," the bank's senior financial analyst Allen Wanna said in a statement issued with the results.
Byblos says it plans to list on the Beirut Stock Exchange in September. The listing is eagerly awaited and the bank's A and B shares are already trading actively on the over the counter (OTC) market.

Total assets at mid-1997 were 37 percent up on a year-to-year basis at 2,562 billion pounds and customer deposits rose 33.6 percent to 2,115 billion pounds over the same period, according to the results.
